d: Edina battles business competitors while Patsy attends a meeting of Menopause Anonymous.
Edina's house, career and personal hygiene have gone to pot while Saffy is away.
Edina tries to organize a book club to get in with the "in" crowd.

Edina is thrilled by the newest addition to her house, a panic room, equipped with champagne, toilet paper and a high-tech surveillance system  Patsy is doing her best to impress new client Minnie Driver.
In an attempt to secure a position among the gentry, a place where people can grow old gracefully, Eddie and Patsy decide to set off for a weekend in the country.
As Saffy prepares to give birth, Patsy's plans to host the prestigious "Style Awards" are dashed by an unexpected arrival.
Edina decides to stay home for Christmas and celebrate the holiday with the baby.
Saffy invites a friend to move in  Patsy learns that, on paper, she has no identity.
The women book the Royal Albert Hall for Jean Durand to perform in  Saffy is upset by her own hypocrisy.

Edina goes to New York to find her long-lost son, Patsy goes to cover fashion week and a rather bizarre marriage takes place. Meanwhile, Saffy observes the world from inside a cupboard to help her career as a writer.
